prompt:
Implement the unfinished `vsandp/client.go` as a dependency-free Go client for the VCF 9.1 vSAN Data Protection `Snapservice.Sessions_create`, `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups_list`, `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups.Snapshots_create$Task`, and `Snapservice.Tasks_get` operations. Keep the implementation in that one file and preserve the exported API already declared there. Before implementing, research those operations in official VMware sources. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer.

Authentication uses, the `vmware-api-session-id` header. `Config.BootstrapToken` is a long-lived operator token that is presented to `Snapservice.Sessions_create` and to nothing else; that operation returns a short-lived working session token which every other operation must carry. Never send an `Authorization` header. Mint the first working token lazily, on the first request that needs one.

`SnapshotProtectionGroups` lists the cluster's protection groups with `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups_list`, then for each returned group starts a one-time snapshot with `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups.Snapshots_create$Task` and polls `Snapservice.Tasks_get` until that task reports `SUCCEEDED` or `FAILED` before moving to the next group. Return one `Result` per group in the order the list response returned them. A `FAILED` task is reported in the `BatchReport`, not returned as an error; a transport failure, a malformed response, or any other non-2xx status aborts the batch with an error.

A working token expires part way through a batch and the appliance then answers `401` with a `Vapi.Std.Errors.Unauthenticated` body. Recover without losing work: mint one replacement token and replay only the rejected request, byte for byte, then carry on where the batch left off. A rejected request never reached the appliance, so nothing that already succeeded may be repeated and no protection group may be snapshotted twice. Give up with an error if the replay is rejected as well, rather than refreshing again. A `Client` is shared by concurrent batches, so one expiry must cost one `Snapservice.Sessions_create` no matter how many in-flight requests it rejected: a caller whose token was already replaced by another goroutine reuses the new token instead of minting its own. `SessionCreates` reports the running total, including the first token.

Match the documented wire shape. Send `Accept: application/json` on every request. A request with no body sends no body and no `Content-Type`; the snapshot create sends `Content-Type: application/json`. The snapshot create is only exposed as a task, so its query string is exactly `vmw-task=true`. `names` is a `form`/`explode` query parameter and is sent once per name in caller order. An unset optional field is omitted entirely and never sent empty: with no name filter the list request has no query string at all, and with no retention the request body is exactly `{"name":"..."}` rather than carrying a null or zero-valued `retention`. Serialize `CreateSpec` properties in this order: `name`, then `retention`, and send both `RetentionPeriod` properties whenever retention is set. Percent-encode identifiers interpolated into paths.

Reject bad input before any request goes out: a missing base URL or bootstrap token, a missing cluster or snapshot name, an empty or repeated entry in the name filter, and a retention without a unit or without a positive duration.

Run `bash protected_tests/verify.sh` to check the implementation. Verification covers exact wire behavior, concurrent token refresh, replay of only the rejected request, exactly-once snapshot creation, optional-field omission, and batch reporting.
